subject: Next steps: procurement path & hosting preferences (PO / card / marketplace)
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@novahealth.com>
Cc: Michael Ortiz <michael.ortiz@novahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: procurement path & hosting preferences (PO / card / marketplace)

Hi Laura / Michael —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so procurement can map to your internal buying rules: 

Summary of fit
- Primary usage: multi-tenant clinical summarization for physician notes (low-latency, HIPAA-constrained).
- Expected steady throughput: ~150 reqs/min with peaks up to ~400 during shift changes.
- Data residency: US-only.

Procurement paths to consider (what you flagged on the call)
1) Card / On-demand (fastest): self-serve hosted API, monthly on card. No contract, ideal for POC and small production.
2) Purchase Order (net-30/60) + Hosted: usage-based billing invoiced monthly; standard commercial terms.
3) Reserved / Dedicated (commit): committed GPU pool with monthly invoice + SLA; requires SOW + PO for reserved capacity.
4) Marketplace (cloud vendor): purchase via AWS Marketplace or Azure Marketplace — options for consolidated billing but sometimes adds procurement lag (vendor approvals).

Open questions from your team (please confirm):
- Which billing path is preferred for initial deployment (Card / PO / Marketplace)?
- Is a signed MSA / DPA required before we can accept a PO (you mentioned legal review could take 2–3 weeks)?
- Would a short-term commit (3 months) to bridge POC -> production make sense operationally?

Action items
- Laura: confirm preferred procurement route and whether procurement needs a pricing worksheet or marketplace listing UID.
- Michael: share procurement contact + PO template if PO route is preferred.
- Hannah: attach a short pricing options table and a one‑page SOW draft (attached).

Attachments: nova_q3_requirements.pdf (your notes), redwood_pricing_options.xlsx (pricing tiers & commit breakpoints).

If it helps, I can prepare two narrow examples: (A) PO for hosted on usage billing with net-30; (B) PO for 6-month reserved capacity with 20% commit discount and SLA. Which should I draft first?

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0122
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@novahealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Ortiz <michael.ortiz@novahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Apr 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: procurement path & hosting preferences (PO / card / marketplace)

Thanks Hannah — useful summary. A few clarifications from procurement: 

- Procurement preference: PO with net-30 for anything >$5k/mo; card OK for POC <$5k.
- Marketplace: Nova prefers marketplace when the vendor is already onboarded to our internal catalog; currently Redwood is not in our AWS/Azure marketplaces, so that would add time.
- Legal: Yes, we need an executed MSA & DPA before we can issue a PO (security needs to sign off). Expect legal review ~2 weeks once we have standard docs.

Next steps for us:
- Michael will introduce me to our procurement lead (Sara Patel) and share PO template.
- Please send a PO-ready pricing worksheet and the MSA + DPA redlines (if any) you typically accept.

Short answers to your Qs:
- Preferred route for initial prod: PO (net-30).
- Commit horizon: 3 months initial is fine; we can evaluate commit discounts after month 2.

Thanks —
Laura
Laura Chen
Director, Clinical Integrations
Nova Health
laura.chen@novahealth.com
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@novahealth.com>, Michael Ortiz <michael.ortiz@novahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Next steps: procurement path & hosting preferences (PO / card / marketplace) — need pricing worksheet for PO

Ben — looping you in to align on commercial packaging. Nova prefers PO (net-30) for initial production; MSA/DPA required before PO. They sign PO >$5k/mo; POC can be card.

Key ask: can you draft a PO-ready pricing worksheet that has two rows: (1) Hosted, usage-based (estimate at 150 rps steady / peak 400) with projected monthly spend and no commit; (2) Dedicated 3-month commit (showing commit discount and expected TCO). Also include marketplace note (not onboarded) so procurement knows it won't be immediate.

Also tag whether we can accept their PO with standard MSA/DPA or if legal needs to negotiate specific redlines.

Thanks —
Hannah
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@novahealth.com>, Michael Ortiz <michael.ortiz@novahealth.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2026 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Next steps: procurement path & hosting preferences (PO / card / marketplace)

Hi Laura / Michael —

Appreciate the clarity. I attached a PO-ready pricing worksheet (redwood_pricing_options.xlsx) and a short one‑page SOW for the 3‑month committed option. Quick highlights below to save time: 

Pricing summary (estimates for initial deployment)
- Hosted, usage (on-demand): est $4,200/mo based on 150 steady / 400 peak token profile. Card acceptable for POC.
- Dedicated, 3-month commit: $10,200/mo (committed capacity sized for peak handling) — includes 20% commit discount vs committed on-demand run. Invoiced monthly via PO.

Procurement/legal notes
- We can accept Nova's standard PO. Please attach your PO template; our contracting team will insert SOW and reference our MSA.
- MSA/DPA: I have attached our standard MSA + DPA (links inside the worksheet). Legal typically needs 7–10 business days for standard redlines. If you have a list of non‑starters (e.g., data residency, breach notification SLAs), flag them now.

Marketplace note
- Onboarding Redwood to AWS/Azure marketplace typically takes 4–6 weeks and is vendor-dependent. If Nova requires marketplace billing for governance reasons, we can start the onboarding in parallel but recommend moving forward with PO for faster time-to-prod.

Proposed immediate next steps
- Laura: send PO template + procurement contact (Sara Patel).
- Michael: confirm expected go-live date (target week of Apr 20) so we size the commit correctly.
- Hannah: I'll sync with legal to prep a redline-friendly MSA copy and confirm the billing cadence for PO.

If helpful, we can do a quick 20-minute call with procurement to walk the worksheet. Happy to schedule.

Best,
Ben Carter
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0173
Attachments: redwood_pricing_options.xlsx (pricing worksheet), redwood_1page_sow.pdf, redwood_msa_dpa_links.txt
